problem: "Water moving steadily along a straight pipe is irrotational" is only true for uniform flow. Real flow in a pipe slows to zero at the wall, so the velocity profile is curved and curl v ≠ 0; a student can carry the wrong picture into fluid mechanics.
fix: "Water moving with the same velocity at every point of a straight pipe (uniform flow) is irrotational; in a real pipe the speed falls to zero at the wall, the profile is curved, and the flow is rotational."

problem: The chart is one straight chain: div test → curl test → set F = ∇φ. Read as a flow, it says a field must pass the div test before a potential is built. Worked example 1 itself finds φ for a field with div F = 6, so the chart contradicts the example and can mislead a student into stopping at a non-zero divergence.
fix: Show the div test as a separate label, not a gate on the φ path. Keep the potential-building path running from the curl test only, and add a note on the div node such as "not solenoidal — a potential may still exist".
